newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania police break up rally, protesters re-group.
newsitem.headline: Albania police break up rally, protesters re-group.

text.p: Riot police in the Albanian port of Vlore tried to break up a protest on Wednesday by depositors demanding refunds for money trapped in failed investment schemes and at least one demonstrator was injured.
Police fired into the air and moved in with water cannon on around 3,000 demonstrators, who threw stones back at them before dispersing.
However the crowd quickly re-grouped and around 5,000 people massed in the centre of the southern city facing a cordon of riot police.

Reuter correspondent Marko Bello saw one man with a serious wound to the head following the initial confrontation, but it was not clear what had caused the injury. He also saw bullet holes in a curbside kiosk and two spent cartridges next to it.
At least 10 people were bundled into police vans.

The Vlore protest was sparked by the collapse on Tuesday of an investment scheme which was hugely popular in the south of the Balkan state. It was the first violent clash seen in Albania since widespread rioting less than two weeks ago.
Investors have begun receiving partial refunds of their stakes in two other failed schemes, but the process was marked by confusion and public frustration.
Refunds were proceeding in Tirana on Wednesday with no indication of any tension. Other regional centres were also reported quiet despite increased police patrols.

Demonstrators, who had poured life savings into the schemes, set fire last month to government buildings around the country, prompting a police crackdown. About 150 people were arrested and prosecutors have threatened long prison terms.
